question.problem:
Which of the following vector-valued functions are differentiable with respect to $t$ on $t\in [0,1]?$

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =⟨t-1,\,{e}^{t},\,{t}^{3}⟩ \\ q(t) & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,\sqrt[3]{2t-1}⟩ \\ r(t) & =⟨3t+2,\,|t|,\,{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
All of these vector-valued functions are defined for all $t\in [0,1].$ 

A function is differentiable on the interval $t\in [0,1]$ if and only if each component is differentiable on that interval.

Let's now consider the functions one by one.

- We differentiate $p(t)$ to find ${p}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,{e}^{t},\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${p}^{′}(t)$ is defined on $[0,1],$ we conclude that $p(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

- Next, we differentiate $q(t)$ to find ${q}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt[3]{2t-1})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{(2t-1)^{2}}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since the third component of this vector, $\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{(2t-1)^{2}}},$ is undefined at $t=\frac{1}{2},$ we conclude that the function $q(t)$ is not differentiable on $[0,1].$

- Finally, since the deviative of the second component $|t|$ of $r(t)$ is undefined at $t=0,$ we conclude that $r(t)$ is not differentiable on this interval.

Therefore, the answer is "$p(t)$ only."

choices.value: None of the functions are differentiable on $t\in [0,1]$
